title: Polymer Chemistry
tagline: Polymer structure and molar mass, step and chain growth, controlled polymerisation, copolymers, chains in solution, characterisation and properties
summary: Polymers — long chains built from small repeating units — range from proteins and DNA to plastics and fibres. This course explains how polymers are made by step-growth, chain-growth and controlled polymerisation, how chains behave in solution, how polymers are characterised, and how structure determines their mechanical, thermal and functional properties.

chapters.title: Polymer structure and molar mass
chapters.summary: Repeat units and nomenclature, tacticity, and number- and weight-average molar masses and dispersity.

chapters.title: Step-growth polymerisation
chapters.summary: Polyesters and polyamides, the Carothers equation, molar-mass distributions and network formation.

chapters.title: Radical chain polymerisation
chapters.summary: Initiation, propagation and termination, the kinetics of chain growth, and chain transfer.

chapters.title: Ionic and controlled polymerisation
chapters.summary: Anionic and cationic polymerisation, living polymerisation, ATRP and RAFT, and ring-opening and coordination polymerisation.

chapters.title: Copolymers
chapters.summary: Reactivity ratios and the Mayo–Lewis equation, and random, alternating, block and graft copolymers.

chapters.title: Polymer chains and solutions
chapters.summary: Random coils and chain dimensions, Flory–Huggins theory, theta solvents and phase separation.

chapters.title: Characterising polymers
chapters.summary: Size-exclusion chromatography, viscometry, light scattering, spectroscopy and thermal analysis.

chapters.title: Mechanical and thermal properties
chapters.summary: Crystallinity and the glass transition, viscoelasticity, rubber elasticity and the strength of polymers.

chapters.title: Functional and biodegradable polymers
chapters.summary: Conducting, stimuli-responsive and biomedical polymers, and polymers designed to degrade.
